items.title: USB-C VBUS and PS1's output both drive 5V
items.detail: J3's VBUS pins and PS1's +VOUT are on the same net with no diode or switch between them. With both plugged in, the USB host and PS1 fight, and PS1 back-feeds the host's VBUS.

evidence.says: J3 A4 and B4 (VBUS) and PS1 pin 3 (+VOUT) are all on 5V; no other part sits between them

items.rule: A connector's power pin and a converter or regulator output on one net, with no diode, ideal diode, or load switch between them, is two sources on one rail

items.title: PS1 has no part file, so the checks don't see it as a 5 V source
items.detail: Without a part file, PS1's +VOUT isn't a power-out pin, so supply.rails can't find two sources on 5V, and 5V's voltage comes only from its name.

evidence.says: PS1 (RAC02-05SK) has no part file in the library

items.needs: A part file for RAC02-05SK with pin 3 as power-out and reg.vout 5 V

items.title: Mark J3 as a power input so its protection is checked
items.detail: J3 brings 5 V onto the board, but the Connectors tab doesn't say so, so power.protection and power.contacts skip it. There's no TVS on 5V.
